prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1167; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed collision in a retail parking lot. Insured reports the other vehicle backed into the insured's rear quarter panel. Police report not filed; both parties exchanged information at the scene. Claimant reported wrist pain at the scene and was transported to urgent care.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. All further contact to go through the attorney's office. Requested medical authorization forms and the complete treatment history from the attorney. Scene photos and insured's statement uploaded to the file. Liability appears probable against the other driver based on the damage pattern, pending witness confirmation.

Entry 3: Attorney's office confirmed claimant was diagnosed with a fracture of the wrist and is in a splint. Surgical consult has been recommended but not yet scheduled. Requested itemized medical bills and records from the treating orthopedic provider. Reserve set for bodily injury exposure pending review of records.

Entry 4: Received preliminary records. Diagnosis confirmed as a distal radius fracture. Treating physician notes indicate a possible return to light duty work within several weeks, but the attorney has indicated the claimant may be off work longer. Scheduled a call with the attorney to discuss documentation of lost wages and the expected course of treatment.

Entry 5: Reviewed the file with supervisor. Liability accepted at a high percentage against the other driver's carrier. Bodily injury evaluation deferred until the claimant completes physical therapy and the surgeon's recommendation is finalized. Next step is a demand package review once counsel submits documentation. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days.
